summary: LLM inference costs scale directly with token usage, where output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens and flagship models cost 16x more than budget tiers for identical workloads. Combining prompt caching (up to 90% off repeated prefixes), semantic caching (30-73% cost reduction), model routing, and output constraints can realistically cut API spend by 50-80% with no quality loss. Prompt caching is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk lever available in 2026, while semantic caching and routing deliver the next tier of savings.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated prompt prefix (system prompts, few-shot examples, static context) so the static portion is billed at a steep discount while producing byte-identical output. The main work is ordering the prompt so the static part actually stays static and dynamic content comes last.
techniques.savings: 41-90% reduction on input tokens for repeated prefixes
techniques.example: Place a 10,000-token system prompt and tool definitions at the start of every request; subsequent calls within the cache TTL bill the prefix at up to 90% off and improve time-to-first-token by 13-31%.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses by meaning rather than exact string match, using vector embeddings to return a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar to a prior one. Requires careful similarity-threshold management to avoid returning confidently wrong answers.
techniques.savings: 30-73% cost reduction (cache hit rates jump from ~18% exact-match to 67-90%)
techniques.example: A support bot maps 'how do I cancel my subscription?' and 'cancel my plan how?' to the same cached answer via embedding similarity, cutting a $47,000/month bill to $12,700 (73% reduction).

techniques.name: Model Routing / Tiering
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, sending simple queries to budget-tier models and reserving flagship models for complex reasoning. A classifier or heuristic decides the tier per request.
techniques.savings: Up to 16x cheaper per workload; typically 60-80% blended cost reduction
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to GPT-3.5/4o-mini and only 5% to GPT-4o, so identical token counts cost $195 instead of $3,250 per million conversations.

techniques.name: Output Length Constraints
techniques.description: Reduces the volume of generated tokens (the most expensive token type) via max_tokens limits, explicit brevity instructions, structured/JSON output, and automated prompt optimization. Output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens.
techniques.savings: 50-80% fewer output tokens (CROP method achieved 80.6% output length reduction)
techniques.example: Set max_tokens and instruct the model to 'respond in under 3 sentences as JSON', cutting output tokens ~50% without losing the needed information.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Removes redundant tokens from prompts and context before sending, using compression tools or rewriting verbose instructions while preserving meaning. Reduces input token count on every call.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved documents through LLMLingua to strip low-information tokens, shrinking a 4,000-token context to ~2,800 before inference.

techniques.name: Context Engineering & RAG Tuning
techniques.description: Sends only the most relevant retrieved chunks instead of stuffing full documents into context, tuning retrieval top-k, chunk size, and reranking to minimize tokens while maintaining answer quality.
techniques.example: Lower RAG top-k from 10 to 4 chunks and add a reranker so the model receives 4 highly relevant passages instead of 10 marginal ones.

techniques.name: Session Context Management & Cache Eviction
techniques.description: Manages conversational memory with hybrid memory, summarization of old turns, and cache eviction/compression so growing chat histories don't inflate per-turn input tokens unboundedly.
techniques.example: Summarize turns older than 10 messages into a short synopsis and evict raw history, keeping per-turn context flat instead of linearly growing.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses keyed on an identical input string, returning instant zero-cost responses for repeated identical queries. Forms the first tier of a multi-tier caching strategy before semantic caching.
techniques.savings: ~15-18% hit rate / cost reduction on repetitive workloads
techniques.example: Hash each prompt and store the result in Redis; identical FAQ queries return the cached answer with zero API cost.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLMs that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity, with pluggable vector stores and eviction policies.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); you pay only for underlying vector DB/infra

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Vector-enabled Redis used for exact-match and semantic caching of LLM responses, with low-latency retrieval and TTL/eviction control for multi-tier caching strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/month; enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Open-source proxy/gateway providing a unified API across 100+ providers with built-in caching, model routing, fallbacks, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering request logging, caching, cost tracking, and rate limiting with a one-line proxy integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier up to 10k requests/month; paid plans from ~$20/month

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching integrations (in-memory, Redis, semantic/GPTCache) plus abstractions for routing and context management.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; LangSmith paid plans from ~$39/user/month

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt compression tool that removes low-information tokens from prompts and context to cut input token counts while preserving meaning.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic caching, model routing, fallbacks, load balancing, and observability across multiple LLM providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans from ~$49/month

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt caching and reorder prompts so static system/few-shot content comes first — up to 90% off repeated input tokens with zero quality loss.
Add a model router that sends simple/high-volume queries to budget-tier models (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and reserves flagship models for complex tasks — up to 16x cheaper per workload.
Set max_tokens limits and instruct models to be concise or return structured JSON to cut expensive output tokens by ~50%.
Drop in an exact-match + semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis via LiteLLM/Helicone) to lift hit rates from ~18% to 67%+ and cut costs 30-73%.
Trim RAG context by lowering top-k and adding reranking so the model only sees the most relevant chunks, cutting input tokens 20-50%.
